title: Margin breach contingency plan + HC & pricing sensitivity (Q3 2025)
summary: Working model to quantify actions if gross margin exhibits sustained degradation vs plan. Combines a phased hiring plan with stepwise pricing changes and elasticity assumptions to show impact on ARR and margin. This is an operational playbook (not final policy) and prioritized by speed-to-impact and reversibility.
key_objective: Hold run-rate gross margin >= 45% while minimizing customer churn and preserving go-to-market momentum.
assumptions: Planned net new ARR for next 4 quarters (base): $12.0M
Average gross cost per inference (weighted across hosted/dedicated/private): $0.00075 per token equivalent
Elasticity baseline: -0.35 revenue % change per +1% price increase for non-enterprise customers (sensible mix)
Enterprise cohort elasticity: -0.05 per +1% price change, assumed slower churn
Hiring lead time: 8 weeks for ICs, 12 weeks for senior hires
Severance/realization lag estimated as 1.1x monthly run-rate when pausing hires and delaying offers
scenarios_summary: Three scenarios modeled: Base (no pricing change, moderate cost reduction initiatives), Price-Uplift (staged +10% then +5% across tiers), and HC-Pause (immediate hiring freeze + selective contract reductions). Outputs: ARR impact, gross margin change, time-to-recover to target margin.

contingency_triggers: Trigger 1: Two consecutive monthly gross margin prints < 43% -> immediate HC hiring freeze for non-critical roles
Trigger 2: Monthly cash burn > 2.2x planned run-rate -> execute targeted contract renegotiations and delay deferred comp payouts
Trigger 3: Net new ARR underperformance > 15% vs plan for consecutive quarter -> stage 1 price uplift (+10%) on self-serve tiers and tighten discounts
recommended_actions: T0 (within 7 days of trigger): Declare HC freeze; stop all non-offer onboarding; communicate to hiring managers
T1 (2-4 weeks): Execute targeted pricing uplift on hosted self-serve tiers (A/B test 10% uplift on 20% traffic), tighten approval on custom discounts
T2 (1-2 months): Defer non-critical infra purchases and delay new datacenter commitments; reprioritize roadmap to high ROI items
T3 (2-3 months): Re-evaluate headcount needs with product prioritization; if margin still below target, consider limited reductions focused on contractors and open requisitions
sensitivity_notes: Elasticities are calibrated from historical Redwood hosted churn patterns and 3rd-party SaaS comps; treat enterprise cohort separately
Price changes should be staged and accompanied by communication and short A/B tests to detect early churn signals
Hiring pauses have asymmetric impact vs cuts; we model a 6-10 week realization lag for immediate savings
Conservative approach prioritizes preserving CS hires to avoid revenue erosion from churn
